sections.h2: Where is Wallingford, CT, and what is around it?
sections.html:
Wallingford is a town in New Haven County on the Quinnipiac River, about 5 miles south of Meriden and 13 miles north of New Haven. It is part of the South Central Connecticut Planning Region, and the 2020 census counted 44,396 residents.

The town covers 39.9 square miles and borders Cheshire, Durham, Hamden, Meriden, Middlefield, North Branford and North Haven. Its communities include Wallingford Center, Yalesville, East Wallingford, Tracy and Quinnipiac, which is partly in North Haven.

Wikipedia describes the town as centrally located between New Haven and Hartford, and Boston and New York City. Which community your house is in is the first thing a buyer will ask.

sections.h2: What is Wallingford's history, from silver to the 1878 tornado?
sections.html:
The Connecticut General Assembly established Wallingford on October 10, 1667, and a group of 38 planters and freemen founded it. By 1675, 40 permanent homes had been built.

The railroad arrived in the 1840s, and the town became known for silver production, with firms such as Hall, Elton and Company and R. Wallace and Sons. Samuel Simpson's company, Simpson, Hall, Miller and Company, later became part of the International Silver Company, based in Meriden.

On August 9, 1878, a tornado struck the town and killed at least 34 people, which Wikipedia describes as the deadliest tornado in Connecticut history. Wallingford's population then grew sharply after World War II, from 16,976 in 1950 to 29,920 in 1960 and 35,714 in 1970.

  • 1667: established by the General Assembly
  • 1840s: railroad arrives
  • 1878: tornado kills at least 34
  • 1960: population reaches 29,920

That postwar jump suggests a good share of the housing dates from those decades. Check the build year on your own record before you describe the house.

Wallingford's biggest employers are the town, a health insurer and several care providers. The ranking below comes from the town's financial report for the year ended June 30, 2023.

The town has several industrial parks, including Barnes, Casimir Pulaski, Centract and MedWay, and an interchange zone near Interstate 91 and Route 68 that supports office parks, research centers and hotels. Bristol-Myers Squibb, once the town's largest taxpayer, moved its operations out in 2017, and its MedWay facility was demolished in 2018.

sections.h2: Which highways, trains and utilities serve Wallingford?
sections.html:
Wallingford is crossed by U.S. Route 5, Interstate 91, Route 15 (the Wilbur Cross Parkway) and Routes 68, 71 and 150. Wallingford station is on the New Haven to Springfield line and is served by the Hartford Line, Amtrak's Northeast Regional and Valley Flyer.

The closest commercial airports are Tweed New Haven in East Haven, Westchester County Airport and Bradley International in Windsor Locks.

The town also runs its own electric utility. The Wallingford Electric Division, established in 1899, is municipally owned and overseen by the Public Utilities Commission of Wallingford. Wikipedia calls it one of Connecticut's few municipal electric utilities. If you are selling, tell buyers your power comes from the town, and have the final bill ready for closing.

Wallingford Public Schools runs two middle schools, Dag Hammarskjold and James H. Moran, and two high schools, Mark T. Sheehan and Lyman Hall. Lyman Hall High School has an agricultural science program.

The town is also home to private schools: Choate Rosemary Hall, a coeducational boarding school, plus Heritage Baptist Academy and Holy Trinity School. Choate is on the employer list, with 299 employees.

Which high school a given street feeds is a district question, and we have not confirmed attendance zones. If you list the house, give buyers the district's contact instead of guessing.

sections.h2: What does a Wallingford seller file with the state when the deed is recorded?
sections.html:
The seller's side files Connecticut Form OP-236, the real estate conveyance tax return, with the Wallingford town clerk. The state Department of Revenue Services says the return and any tax are due at recording, and the tax applies when consideration is $2,000 or more.

Wallingford's code on the form is 148. Where the town takes electronic filings, myCTREC handles the return and payment. Otherwise a paper return and check go to the clerk. The clerk then sends the return to the state.

Exemption listed by the stateShort version
Principal residence in lieu of foreclosureDeed given to a lender instead of foreclosure
Principal residence, price too lowPrice cannot cover the mortgages and priority liens
SpousesProperty conveyed between spouses
Deed restricted affordable housingAll units deed restricted
Tax deedInstrument is a tax deed

Each exemption needs the right code on the return, or the town clerk cannot accept it. Your closing attorney should pick the right one. The DRS page has the full list.

sections.h2: What historic places are in Wallingford?
sections.html:
Ten buildings and districts in Wallingford are on the National Register of Historic Places, and the Wallingford Center Historic District was added on December 2, 1993. The old Wallingford railroad station was listed on November 19, 1993, and the Samuel Simpson House on June 18, 1986.

Other listings include the Nehemiah Royce House, the Samuel Parsons House, the Theophilus Jones House and the Center Street Cemetery. Choate Rosemary Hall's campus holds the Paul Mellon Arts Center, designed by I. M. Pei.

Lyman Hall, a physician born in Wallingford in 1724 who signed the Declaration of Independence for Georgia, gave his name to one of the town's two high schools. Moses Yale Beach, who owned the New York Sun, was also born here.

  • If your house is inside the Wallingford Center Historic District, ask the town what rules apply to outside changes before you plan work.
  • Buyers of a listed property may ask what restrictions come with it, so have the answer ready.

sections.h2: How does a cash sale work for a Wallingford house?
sections.html:
A cash sale in Wallingford works without a lender, so you can pick a closing date once title work is clear. Tell us about the house, and we give you an offer based on its current condition, with no obligation to accept.

It can suit an inherited home, a rental with tenants in place, or a house that needs work on the roof, windows or systems.

  • You do not clean out or repair before an offer
  • You can turn the offer down at no cost
  • You choose among closing dates that fit your move

We did not confirm any Wallingford permit, rental or code enforcement rules from an official town page, so we have left them out. The town's website at wallingfordct.gov or its offices can tell you what applies to your property.

faqs.q: What county is Wallingford, CT in?
faqs.a: Wallingford is in New Haven County, in the South Central Connecticut Planning Region.

faqs.q: How many people live in Wallingford?

faqs.a: The Wallingford Electric Division, a municipal utility established in 1899, provides electricity to the town.

faqs.q: What is Wallingford's code on the Connecticut conveyance tax form?
faqs.a: The code is 148. The seller's side files Form OP-236 with the town clerk at recording.

faqs.q: Is Wallingford on a train line?
faqs.a: Yes. Wallingford station is on the New Haven to Springfield line, served by the Hartford Line and Amtrak.

faqs.q: Which companies employ the most people in Wallingford?
faqs.a: The town government (1,478 employees) and Anthem BC/BS (1,225) lead the list in the town's 2023 financial report.

faqs.q: Do I need to renovate before selling for cash?
faqs.a: No. A cash offer is made on the house as it is, with no required repairs.
